forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: West of England Joint Committee reports exhausted general reserves; budget needs Combined Authority subsidy
news_drafts.lead:
The West of England Joint Committee's general reserves are exhausted, and its budget can be balanced only with a subsidy from the West of England Combined Authority, according to a report to a joint meeting of the two bodies on 23 October 2026.

The statement is in the risk section of the report on the Joint Committee's budget and change requests, item 08 on the agenda. It says the position "links to the ongoing reducing general reserves position, which is now exhausted and requires a subsidy from the Combined Authority to balance".

The report as verified gives no figure for the size of the subsidy or for the reserves at earlier dates. It does not set out in the material seen here when the Joint Committee's reserves ran out.

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: 20261016 West of England Combined Authority - Audit Findings Report 25-26 - Final
findings.headline: The Authority's net cost of services increased by over 45% from the prior year, which the auditor says increased the number of samples needed.
findings.detail: The auditor links the increase in spending to a larger number of samples in some areas, which added audit work. The auditor describes this as a driver of the delay in concluding the audit.
findings.matters: A rise in net cost of services of this size is a change in scale that finance directors and lenders will want to see reflected in reserves and budget planning.
findings.figures: Increase in net cost of services: over 45%
findings.quote: increase of over 45% in net cost of services

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: 20261016 West of England Combined Authority - Audit Findings Report 25-26 - Final
findings.headline: Grant Thornton is satisfied that the Authority has made proper arrangements for economy, efficiency and effectiveness in its use of resources.
findings.detail: The auditor's value for money work covers governance, financial sustainability, and improving economy, efficiency and effectiveness. The detailed commentary is in the separate Auditor's Annual Report presented to Audit Committee on 28 September 2026.
findings.matters: A clean value for money conclusion is the auditor's assessment that governance and financial sustainability arrangements are adequate, which lenders and peer councils look for.
findings.quote: We are satisfied that the Authority has made proper arrangements to secure economy, efficiency and effectiveness in its use of resources.

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: 20261016 West of England Combined Authority - Audit Findings Report 25-26 - Final
findings.headline: The auditor recommends independent review of journals posted by senior finance officers as best practice to address management override of controls.
findings.detail: Management override of controls was assessed as a significant risk, and the auditor reports that no material misstatement arose from management bias. The auditor has raised a best practice point for the Authority on journal review.
findings.matters: Journal controls over senior finance officers are a standard governance check that other finance directors will compare against their own journal review arrangements.
findings.quote: We have raised a best practice point for the Authority.

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: 20261016 West of England Combined Authority - Audit Findings Report 25-26 - Final
findings.headline: Auditors found that leavers' accounts could remain active indefinitely, which the auditor reports as a control deficiency with no mitigating controls.
findings.detail: The auditor's testing of leavers' access found instances of leavers being removed inappropriately late in the year. The auditor reports that without mitigating controls, their account could theoretically remain active indefinitely.
findings.matters: IT access control deficiencies on a finance system are a common audit finding that other finance directors will want to check against their own leaver processes.
findings.quote: their account could theoretically remain active indefinitely

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: 20261016 West of England Combined Authority - Audit Findings Report 25-26 - Final
findings.headline: The Authority's net pension liability on its balance sheet is £0.08 million, after gross pension liabilities of £30.537 million, gross pension assets of £37.707 million, and a £7.25 million asset ceiling adjustment.
findings.detail: The auditor identified a small number of inconsistencies and missing disclosures between the Statement of Accounts and the IAS 19 reports, which management has agreed to amend. The auditor found no other issues with the valuation.
findings.matters: Pension liability and asset ceiling figures determine the balance sheet exposure to the Avon Pension Fund, which lenders and finance directors compare across authorities.
findings.figures: Net pension liability: £0.08 million; gross pension liability: £30.537 million; gross pension assets: £37.707 million; asset ceiling adjustment: £7.25 million
findings.quote: as reflected in its Balance Sheet as the net pension liability £0.08 million

daily_post.headline: The audit committee's 14 September 2026 meeting was inquorate, with eight members present, so no formal decisions were made
daily_post.lead: Repeated inquorate meetings mean that audit items, including financial and risk matters, are not being formally decided, which a finance director would weigh when assessing the council's governance.
